One-sentence judgment: brownfield redevelopment specialists and site managers are not "running approvals," but rather develop and drive executable plans for the cleanup and reuse of contaminated land: identifying contamination sources, organizing site investigation and risk assessment, estimating cleanup costs, designing and implementing risk control and remediation measures, applying for funding and coordinating construction and redevelopment, and being responsible for safety, quality, and compliance. The U.S. side corresponds to O*NET-SOC 11-9199.11, listed as Job Zone Four (SVP 7.0 to below 8.0) and marked Bright Outlook. The core boundary is that the official duties explicitly state "does not include sites where the extent of contamination is sufficient to constitute a Superfund site," so highly contaminated sites included in the national priorities list are handled by the corresponding procedures and entities; nor may you issue legally binding investigation, risk assessment, or effectiveness assessment conclusions in place of a qualified institution.

Signals to keep exploring: your interest in "what this land was used for in the past, where the contamination comes from, how contaminants migrate, whether remediation targets are achievable, and whether cost and schedule are controllable" is greater than in "whether the project is high-profile"; you are willing to check investigation data, regulatory standards, remediation technologies, and cost estimates together, and can insist on advancing with evidence and procedure when the demands of multiple parties (owner, contractor, regulator, community) conflict; you accept that plans will be revised as new data arrives and are willing to document the reasons for each change.

Conditions for pausing high-cost investment first: you have not yet fully participated under supervision in a closed loop from preliminary site investigation, risk screening, remediation option comparison, cost estimation, and construction and acceptance support to post-closure management, or you only want to give conclusions quickly and are unwilling to verify data sources and applicable standards; also, do not treat "studied an environmental major" or "can read drawings" as proof that you can independently sign site investigation, risk assessment, or effectiveness assessment conclusions.

Education, qualifications, and signing authority must be verified separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone Four (SVP 7.0 to below 8.0), and among respondents 77% consider a bachelor's degree necessary, 9% consider a post-baccalaureate certificate necessary, and 9% consider a master's degree necessary; in mainland China, activities such as site investigation, risk assessment, risk control and remediation, and their effectiveness assessment shall be carried out by units with the corresponding professional capability, and the commissioned unit is responsible for the truthfulness, accuracy, and completeness of the reports it issues; the list for construction land soil contamination risk control and remediation is formulated and published by the provincial ecological environment department together with the natural resources and other departments; the authority for investigation, review, plan filing, and acceptance of a specific project is determined by applicable regulations and the competent department, and does not arise from education or personal experience by itself.

One sentence: this is an interdisciplinary management position centered on site investigation and risk assessment, risk control and remediation plans, cost and funding, multi-party compliance coordination, and redevelopment coordination, and its outputs are verifiable plans, estimates, monitoring records, and acceptance records, not legal conclusions or investment decisions. The work of this occupation can be divided into three categories: first, investigation and assessment (identifying contamination sources and historical uses, organizing or reviewing site investigation and human health and environmental risk assessment, verifying whether contaminants exceed risk control standards, and defining remediation targets and scope); second, plan and implementation management (comparing risk control and remediation technologies, estimating costs and schedules, applying for funding, organizing construction and monitoring, tracking progress and handling anomalies, and supporting effectiveness assessment and post-closure management); third, compliance and redevelopment coordination (liaising with the competent department and review procedures, preparing reports and communication materials, coordinating owners, contractors, communities, and other parties, and translating investigation and remediation conclusions into reusable land use conditions). All three share the same responsibility chain centered on the site and on evidence and procedure.
Investigation and risk assessment

Collect historical use and production information → identify potential contamination sources and migration pathways → organize or review the site environmental investigation → verify whether contaminants exceed soil contamination risk control standards → organize or review the risk assessment → define risk control and remediation targets.
Plan and implementation management

Compare risk control and remediation technologies → estimate cleanup and redevelopment costs and prepare budgets → apply for and match project funding → organize construction, monitoring, and contaminated soil transport → track progress, handle anomalies, and document → support effectiveness assessment and post-closure management.

Liaise with the competent department and review procedures, prepare reports communicating redevelopment needs and progress, coordinate owners, contractors, regulators, and communities, and translate investigation and remediation conclusions into land use conditions and redevelopment milestone plans.

Environmental scientists and specialists can also investigate, analyze risks, and propose prevention plans, and are not limited to sampling and monitoring; brownfield positions lean toward cleanup and redevelopment coordination, and actual overlapping duties are verified per project, and permits cannot be swapped.
Core purpose

Under regulatory standards and land use requirements, translate the contamination conditions and risks of a contaminated site into executable, acceptable risk control and remediation plans and redevelopment arrangements so that the site can be safely and compliantly reused.
Main objects and basis

The objects are the site's historical uses and contamination sources, site investigation and risk assessment data, risk control and remediation plans, costs and funding, construction and monitoring records, and redevelopment plans; the basis is soil contamination risk control standards and related technical specifications, environmental impact assessment and permit requirements, the competent department's review and filing procedures, and applicable environmental laws and regulations.
Core process

Identify contamination sources, organize investigation and risk assessment, prepare and compare remediation plans, estimate costs and apply for funding, organize construction and monitoring, support effectiveness assessment and post-closure management, and prepare reports and coordinate parties.
Main outputs

Site contamination identification and investigation results, risk assessment and remediation target statements, risk control and remediation plans and cost estimates, funding applications and budget materials, construction and monitoring records, effectiveness assessment and post-closure management support materials, and redevelopment progress reports and land use condition statements.
Responsible parties

China's current Ecological Environment Code Article 438: units engaged in related investigation, assessment, risk control, remediation, and post-closure management shall have the corresponding professional capability; the commissioned unit is responsible for the truthfulness, accuracy, and completeness of reports and is responsible for the results of the activities as agreed. This is not a uniform license for all personnel or the power to issue "legal conclusions." Articles 439—442 separately address the party responsible for contamination, the land use right holder when responsibility cannot be determined, succession, and dispute determination, and do not automatically treat the site manager as the party responsible for contamination.
Authority and approval

Construction land: 454, the local ecological environment department together with natural resources organizes review of investigation reports; 455—456, risk reports are submitted to the provincial level and review and list inclusion are organized; 459, for sites on the remediation list, plans are combined with territorial spatial planning and filed with the local ecological environment department; 460, the responsible party separately commissions the effectiveness assessment and files it; 461, the provincial level together with relevant departments reviews and removes sites from the list. Filing, review, approval, and engineering acceptance differ, and specific changes are verified against applicable rules. Ecological Environment Code 435, disclosure of the site conditions and protective measures on the construction notice board; 436, the construction unit formulates a transport plan and submits the time, method, route, quantity, destination, and final disposal measures in advance to the ecological environment departments of the location and the receiving location; if it is hazardous waste, it is disposed of per applicable rules, and not all contaminated soil is automatically hazardous waste, nor is there uniform approval reporting.

paragraphs: This page compares brownfield redevelopment specialists and site managers with five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: career direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which direction each preference better suits. Adjacent directions are described according to their own official occupation descriptions, and do not mean trade names are interchangeable.

Evidence note: the career directions and core outputs are based on the official descriptions of O*NET 11-9199.11 and the adjacent entries (U.S. basis); the qualifications, authorization, and compliance requirements of adjacent trades must be verified separately under their own jurisdictions, and this page does not present any direction as a shortcut to a career change.

The table below compares the directional differences between brownfield redevelopment specialists and site managers and adjacent trades; the basis for judgment is the main outputs, what the role is responsible for, and the training required, rather than the similarity of trade names.
Environmental Scientists and Specialists
Conduct environmental sampling, monitoring, and data analysis and environmental impact assessment, with outputs mainly monitoring data and assessment reports.

Environmental scientists focus on scientific sampling and data analysis; brownfield redevelopment specialists and site managers build on their results to coordinate remediation plans, costs, and redevelopment procedures and are responsible for project progress.
If you prefer sampling and analysis, examine environmental scientists and specialists first; if you prefer coordinating plans and projects, examine this occupation first.
Civil Engineers
Responsible for site engineering, foundation and structural design and calculation, with outputs mainly design documents and calculation reports.

Civil engineers are responsible for engineering design and structural safety and need an engineering license; this occupation is responsible for plan coordination and compliance and does not carry structural design seals.
If you prefer design and calculation, examine civil engineers first; if you prefer remediation and redevelopment coordination, examine this occupation first.
Construction Managers
Organize on-site construction, schedule, cost, and safety, with outputs mainly construction plans and site management records.
Construction managers focus on construction organization and on-site execution; this occupation determines cleanup and remediation targets upstream and coordinates procedures and funding.
If you prefer organizing construction on site, examine construction managers first; if you prefer plan and compliance coordination, examine this occupation first.
Hazardous Materials Removal Workers
Remove and dispose of hazardous substances on site under protective conditions, with outputs mainly removal records and disposal certificates.

Hazardous materials removal workers perform on-site work and need the corresponding training and protection; this occupation defines the work scope and acceptance requirements and does not replace their on-site operations.
If you prefer on-site removal work, examine hazardous materials removal workers first; if you prefer plans and management, examine this occupation first.
Compliance Officers
Inspect and assess whether an organization complies with laws and regulations and drive corrective action, with outputs mainly inspection conclusions and rectification requirements.

Compliance officers address organizational compliance systems and inspections; this occupation addresses the contamination and remediation procedures of a specific site and requires understanding both environmental technology and regulations.
If you prefer compliance inspections, examine compliance officers first; if you prefer site technical and plan coordination, examine this occupation first.
Cost Estimators
Prepare engineering and project cost estimates, with outputs mainly estimate reports and bid budgets.
Cost estimators focus on costing methods; this occupation must incorporate remediation technical plans, regulatory requirements, and schedule into estimates and funding arrangements.
If you prefer cost estimating, examine cost estimators first; if you prefer technical plans and funding coordination, examine this occupation first.

Conclusion: the basis for choosing a direction is the main outputs, what the role is responsible for, and the training required, not how similar the names are; once the direction is set, you should verify item by item the target position's qualification and professional capability requirements, the range of documents that may be signed, data and professional responsibility, and project safety and compliance requirements, and keep written confirmation.

subject.name: Brownfield redevelopment specialists and site managers
subject.summary: The entry on this page corresponds to brownfield redevelopment specialists and site managers (U.S. side O*NET-SOC 11-9199.11): developing and driving plans for the cleanup and reuse of contaminated land — identifying contamination sources, organizing or reviewing site investigation and risk assessment, comparing risk control and remediation technologies, estimating costs and applying for funding, coordinating construction and monitoring, supporting effectiveness assessment and post-closure management, and liaising with review procedures; the work routinely involves data and standards verification, multi-party regulatory communication, and project coordination, and its duties do not include sites whose contamination is sufficient to constitute a Superfund site, nor do they replace legally binding conclusions issued by qualified units.
